inventory.caption: *Commodity intelligence and its engineered environment.* Training develops general-purpose capabilities; the harness turns reasoning into action. The engineer maintains the system knowledge and mechanisms that guide the agent, constrain its actions, and evaluate whether selected results may be accepted. Training data need not all be public.
inventory.conversion: Native editable TikZ and live-text SVG reauthored together from the author specification.
inventory.svg_title: Commodity intelligence and its engineered environment
inventory.svg_description: Training data, including open-source code and other data, is used in pretraining and post-training to produce foundation-model weights. A deployed model provides four properties, each paired with an engineering implication, while the harness supplies tool action, context management, interposition and parallel execution. The agent changes an existing system. The engineered environment supplies guidance and governs selected actions and results. The engineer principally engineers and maintains that environment, with training or fine-tuning shown as an optional route.

inventory.caption: *Representation and the reasoning horizon.* When relevant state cannot all remain active, it must be preserved elsewhere and recovered. Raw implementation can demand repeated reconstruction; purposeful abstraction can reduce that burden, making work cheaper and sometimes bringing more demanding tasks within the system’s reasoning horizon.
inventory.conversion: TikZ diagram; inspect SVG and chapter/receipt
inventory.svg_description:
At sufficient scale a task requires more reasoning state than a finite reasoner can
    keep active, so some state must be reconstructed. A branch node, representation matters, states that the
    representation the reasoner works through determines how much of that state must be reconstructed. The
    figure forks from that node. On the left, raw implementation as the working substrate carries a large
    active state, forces repeated reconstruction, and easily loses relevant structure, ending in churn. On
    the right, a purposeful abstraction keeps the question-relevant state smaller, lowers the reconstruction
    burden, and sustains longer coherent reasoning. A causal spine at the foot reads: finite active state,
    reconstruction unavoidable, representation determines burden.

inventory.caption: *From substrate to method.* Finite reasoning state creates the Representation Problem; probabilistic autonomous work creates the Enforcement Problem.
inventory.conversion: TikZ diagram; inspect SVG and chapter/receipt
inventory.svg_description:
Two derivations run left to right. In the first, a finite working state raises the
    representation problem, which modeling addresses in Chapter 2. In the second, probabilistic productive
    work over observable, interposable seams raises the enforcement problem, which alignment addresses in Chapter 3. These are the two core activities Chapter 1 derives; Chapter 4 puts them in motion as the MAGE method.
